text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages (70-140 words each), each with two variants for changed quantity, reordered and moved negation.

passages.source_passage: Board update, March 2024: The Kanembo Primary Nutrition Initiative now serves hot midday meals in 46 schools across the Dassara district, reaching roughly 11,200 pupils each term. Attendance on feeding days rose by 14 percent compared with the same quarter last year. Procurement from local women's cooperatives covered three quarters of our grain needs, which kept costs below budget. Head teachers reported that pupils who did not eat breakfast at home were the most regular attenders. However, deliveries to the four schools beyond the Mborou river did not arrive during the July floods, and pupils there went without meals for nine school days. The committee has yet to approve a reserve stock for those sites, and we ask the board to consider this at the next meeting.

passages.source_passage: Monitoring report, Quarter 2, 2023. The Lirenne Community Counselling Service held 1,340 individual sessions and 58 group sessions across its three drop-in centres. Of the 412 new clients screened, 61 percent were women and most were referred by teachers or clinic nurses. Average waiting time for a first appointment fell from 19 days to eight. At the Hollin Gate centre counsellors did not meet the target of two supervision hours per week, but the other two centres did. The clinical supervisor there was on leave for six weeks. Follow-up calls showed that clients who completed at least five sessions reported lower distress scores than those who left early. The service does not yet collect outcome data from group participants, and this gap should be addressed before the annual review.

passages.source_passage: Trainer's guide, Session 3. When you visit a household for the Tamaru Nets for Every Sleeper campaign, count sleeping spaces first, not people. We allocate one net for every two sleepers, rounding up, so a home with five sleepers receives three nets. Nets that are not recorded in the register should be reported to your supervisor the same day. Remind families that a new net should be aired in the shade for 24 hours before use and should never be dried in direct sunlight. In last year's round, volunteers in Bekova ward found that about 30 percent of old nets had holes larger than a thumb. Collect those nets only if the family agrees; we are not running a replacement scheme this year, and no household should feel pressured.

passages.source_passage: Board update, September 2023. The Ruvenzi District Health Partnership now supports 214 community health workers in 38 villages, up from 180 at the start of the year. Each worker visits an average of 22 households per week. Worker registers are checked monthly by district supervisors and each quarter by clinic nurses. Facility records show that 72 percent of referred women attended at least four antenatal visits. Stock-outs of oral rehydration salts did not affect the northern villages, but the southern villages were without supplies for most of August. Stipends were paid late in two months because the district treasury had not released its share of funds. Management does not recommend expanding to new villages, and recommends stabilising the payment system first.

passages.source_passage: Board update, January 2025. The Sefton Vale Evening Literacy Network ran 27 classes in church halls and community centres during the autumn term, with 389 adult learners enrolled. Two thirds of learners were women over 40, many of whom had never attended formal school. By December, 156 learners had passed the Level 1 reading assessment, compared with 98 in the previous autumn. Retention was weaker in the rural classes than in the town classes. Learners in the rural classes could not travel after dark in winter, so sessions moved to Saturday mornings. We did not renew the partnership with the Marlow Street library because the venue was hard for wheelchair users to reach. Volunteer tutors gave an estimated 2,100 hours, and the board is asked to approve a small travel fund for them.

passages.source_passage: Monitoring report, long rains season 2024. The Ombasi Farmer Field School Network enrolled 64 groups with an average of 25 members each, of whom 58 percent were women. In each cluster, lead farmers mentored new members while extension officers supervised the facilitators. Yields averaged about 1.4 tonnes per hectare on improved-seed plots, against 0.9 tonnes on control plots. Facilitators did not record pest scouting data for 11 groups, but did record rainfall for all groups, so the pest management results are incomplete. Seed deliveries to the Kiraso cluster were delayed, so those groups planted not with the first rains but three weeks later. Farmers there were frustrated, and attendance at the following two sessions dropped sharply.

passages.source_passage: Monitoring report, October to December 2023. Caregivers in the Nyandeko Home Visiting Programme made 2,870 home visits to 315 clients living with HIV across nine wards. Ninety-one percent of clients on treatment had a documented adherence check at least once a month. Volunteers delivered food parcels to 120 households with children under five and hygiene kits to bedridden clients. Two volunteers resigned, and the remaining 43 now carry heavier caseloads. Clients who were not visited monthly missed more clinic appointments than clients who received regular visits. In Mabango ward, caregivers did not have gloves for most of November, but they did have soap and basic dressing supplies. The programme has not integrated tuberculosis screening into home visits, although the district clinic has offered training this quarter.

passages.source_passage: Board update, June 2024. The Harrowgate Youth Skills Centre graduated 132 trainees from its six-month courses in welding, tailoring and solar installation. Within three months of graduating, 64 percent were in paid work or running their own businesses. Solar installation graduates found jobs faster than tailoring graduates, largely because two regional contractors recruited directly from the centre. Employers rated graduates' punctuality higher than their technical skills. Female enrolment in welding remains low, with only 9 women in a cohort of 40. The centre did not receive the promised equipment grant, but did receive a smaller donation of hand tools, so trainees shared power tools in groups of four. Fees were held this year not because costs fell but because the board asked us to protect access.

passages.source_passage: Mid-term evaluation summary. Between April 2022 and March 2024, the Koro Basin Cash Support Programme made monthly transfers of 45 dollars to 6,800 households affected by repeated drought. Household food consumption scores improved for 70 percent of recipients, and the share of families eating only one meal a day fell from 31 percent to 12 percent. Transfers were made by mobile money in most villages and by cash in the remote highland villages. Evaluators did not find evidence that transfers raised local market prices, but they did find delays in registration. Women-headed households were not consulted on transfer timing in the first year but were consulted in the second, after several reported that payments arrived after school fees were due. Targeting errors were estimated at under 8 percent.

passages.source_passage: Monitoring report, first half of 2025. The Pellow Bay Community Playgroup Network ran 52 weekly playgroups for children aged two to five, with average attendance of 14 children per session. Caregivers attended alongside their children in 80 percent of sessions, which is above our target of 70 percent. Facilitators reported that boys used the building blocks more often than girls, so play corners now rotate every 20 minutes. Developmental screening was not carried out at the six island sites but was completed at all mainland sites. The screening nurse was unable to travel to the islands during the storm season. Most groups did not have enough picture books, but they did have locally made toys from the parents' workshop. Parents asked for sessions on Saturdays, not weekdays.
